_comment: Hand-decided destinations for the Drupal-era URL space, which WordPress never redirected either — see data/legacy-404s.json for the Google Search Console evidence. Kept separate from legacy-revista-aliases.json, which is a frozen crawl of the WordPress /la-revista/ space and must stay verbatim. Consumed by scripts/build-legacy-redirects.ts.

revistaSlugAliases._comment: Drupal-era edition slugs that drifted before WordPress, so they are absent from the WordPress crawl. Applied under /content/, /la-revista/ and /revistavamos/.

exact._comment: Drupal page paths with a single obvious counterpart on the new site.
exact._comment2: Corrections to what the /content/ and /la-revista/ wildcards below would otherwise do. The leading spaces are real: old pages linked the edition with a stray space, which arrives as %20 and survives the wildcard's passthrough into a 404. consejos-para-tu-primer-ano-misionero was never an edition on the new site.
exact._comment3: Drupal pager artefacts, from the 2026-08-29 Search Console "Page with redirect" export. The pager both cut the edition slug at a hyphen (`/la-revista/la-?page=5`) and served the page number as a path segment (`/la-revista/la-solteria/5/`); each truncated slug pairs with its numbered twin crawled the same day, which is how the intended edition is known. Without these the hand-written /la-revista/:path* wildcard 301s all five into a 404.

wildcards._comment: /content/<slug> was Drupal's alias for a magazine edition — the same slug space /la-revista/ later used, so it gets the same passthrough rule. Emitted after the exact rules above so the aliases win.
Drupal resource detail pages. Per-slug rules pointing at the actual document are emitted first where the asset survived; this catches the rest.
The VAMOS course sections have no per-section counterpart; the material they linked now lives on /recursos/.

`/larevista/` without the hyphen — a Drupal-era spelling Google still crawls, in the same relationship to /la-revista/ as /cursovamos/ is to /curso-vamos/. The hyphenated wildcard does not match it, so it 404s.

Drupal resource detail pages under their other prefix — `/recursos-misioneros/<slug>` sat beside `/recurso/<slug>` and `/recursos-movilicemos/`, and is the only one of the three the wildcards missed. Same treatment: the per-slug document rules are emitted first where the asset survived, this catches the rest.
